invented.quote: Some played once. Many came back.
invented.why: The brief only says 60 people played across 140 sessions, which proves at least one person played more than once, not that some played once and many came back.
The brief does not mention whether or how often the playtest sessions resulted in changes to the game.

invented.quote: where strangers sat down and played it without knowing anything about it.
invented.why: The brief only says the creator took the game to two conventions, not who played it there or what they knew about it beforehand.
The brief states the game has 23 ratings on the board game ratings site, not that all 23 raters have actually played the game.

invented.quote: every one of them has played it
invented.why: The brief does not confirm that everyone who rated the game on the website had played it.

invented.quote: leaves about $5,450 for the campaign's fees and costs along the way.
invented.why: The brief does not specify what the remaining funds after printing and shipping will be used for.

invented.quote: So the goal isn't a guess. It's the factory quote plus shipping plus a margin.
invented.why: The brief gives the funding goal and the costs, but does not state how the creator calculated or arrived at the $28,000 goal.

invented.quote: Over 140 sessions, the players have told me the same.
invented.why: The brief does not mention what feedback playtesters gave during the 140 sessions.
The brief only states that the game is about seeing a lighthouse keeper's family through a winter, without mentioning tending a lamp as part of the game.
